why: A (universes at 0) has three conjuncts: isEquivalence_of_isIso (an IsIso morphism of the category EP is an equivalence), IsEquivalence.comp, and proposition_10_1_5 (if F ≃ G, then F is an equivalence iff G is). B states (E1) for B's own componentwise notion of isomorphism, IsIsoB (an EpFunctor G inverse to F on objects and on morphisms), and states (E2) and (E3) with ≃ in either direction. A ⇒ B: (E1) bundles X and Y as objects of EP and turns G into an IsIso instance with EpFunctor.ext; (E2) is immediate; (E3) is one half of the iff, applied to F → G or to G → F. B ⇒ A: (E1) reads G off IsIso.out and gets its four componentwise equations by congrArg, as the project's proof does; the iff of (E3) is two applications of B's (E3), with Or.inl and Or.inr. The two sides say the same thing. The only differences are packaging: IsIso in EP versus componentwise inverses, and the iff versus the one-way implication with ≃ symmetric.
